title: Measuring the Inflammation

patient.name: Mr Chia Hock Lai
patient.presenting_complaint: Recent cataract surgery; doctor wants an aqueous flare measurement to check post-operative inflammation

history.hpc: Mr Chia had left eye cataract surgery about a week ago. The eye is still slightly red and the doctor has ordered a flare test to objectively assess inflammation. He says: 'After my operation the eye still a bit red, doctor want check the inflammation inside.' No severe pain or sudden vision drop. The OT must perform the laser flare test and document the flare value.
history.pmhx: Left cataract surgery 1 week ago. Hypertension.
medications: Post-op steroid and antibiotic eye drops (left eye)
history.social_hx: Lives with wife. Compliant with post-op drops. Non-smoker.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Left eye mild residual conjunctival redness; anterior chamber to be quantified by flare test

investigations.flare_test: Laser flare photometry performed on the left (operated) eye, with the right eye as a baseline comparison. The flare value reflects the protein concentration (inflammation) in the anterior chamber. The operated eye shows a mildly raised flare value consistent with expected early post-operative inflammation, lower than an acute uveitis level. Documented for the doctor.
investigations.measurement_quality: Good alignment in the anterior chamber; repeat readings consistent.

diagnosis: Mildly raised aqueous flare in the operated eye, consistent with expected early post-operative inflammation, providing the doctor an objective measure to guide steroid drop tapering. The OT competency is correct flare measurement and documentation; the treatment decision is the doctor's.

immediate: Confirm the indication (post-op inflammation assessment) and which eye to measure
Explain the non-contact flare test and position the patient correctly
Measure the operated eye and the fellow eye for comparison, taking consistent repeat readings
Record the flare value(s) and note they reflect anterior chamber inflammation
Document diagnosis, indication, RE/LE, and the flare findings for the doctor
Avoid adjusting medications yourself — present the result for the doctor's decision
follow_up: Doctor to use the flare value to guide steroid drop tapering and follow-up timing
Continue post-op drops as currently prescribed until the doctor advises
Repeat flare measurement at review if ordered to track the trend
patient_education: Explain the test measures inflammation inside the eye after surgery, painlessly
Reassure him that some inflammation is expected early after cataract surgery
Advise him to keep using his drops as prescribed until the doctor changes them
Tell him the warning signs (increasing pain, redness, or vision drop) and to return if they occur

key_points: Confirms the recent surgery and the indication for the flare test
Confirms the operated eye and current post-op drops
Checks for warning symptoms (severe pain, vision drop)
Explains the procedure to the patient
Performs flare photometry on the operated eye with the fellow eye for comparison
Ensures correct alignment and consistent repeat readings
Records the flare value as a measure of anterior chamber inflammation
Documents diagnosis, indication, RE/LE, and findings
Recognises a mildly raised flare as consistent with expected early post-op inflammation
Understands the flare value helps guide steroid tapering
Distinguishes expected post-op flare from a higher acute-uveitis level
Knows the OT role is measurement/documentation, not treatment
Produces consistent flare readings and documents them clearly
Does not adjust medications and presents the result to the doctor
Explains the test and reassures the patient
Advises on continuing drops and warning signs
